newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico still undecided on tortilla price hikes.
newsitem.headline: Mexico still undecided on tortilla price hikes.

text.p: Mexican Agriculture Minister Francisco Labastida Ochoa said Tuesday the government was still undecided on whether corn-pancake tortilla prices should be raised.
"What is being examined, and there is no decision on this, is if the price of tortilla be altered and to what extent," Labastida said in an interview.
Labastida said additional factors had arisen in recent months that had to be taken into account concerning the price of Mexico's favourite staple which is eaten more widely than bread.
For example, he said salaries paid by tortilla manufacturers had risen in the recent round of government, business and labour sector wage hike accords.
Tortillas are priced at 1.40 peso per kilo and heavily subsidized by the federal government to make sure the Mexican population has cheap access to a fundamental staple in their daily diet.

Also, any hike in tortilla prices impacts inflation via the consumer price index, which is why increases have to be carefully planned. Tortillas make up a sizeable segment of the basic basket of goods too.
Labastida said government subsidies for tortillas in 1997 will amount to 4.5 billion pesos, some 2 billion pesos less than the expected final outcome for subsidies for 1996.
Labastida said high corn prices in the first half of the year were partly to blame for the high subsidies this year.
